did_you_know.text: Did you know? The people cried all night, emphasizing the depth of their despair and complaint after hearing the spies' report.
Did you know? The complaint "would that we had died in the land of Egypt or in this wilderness" is one of many expressions of distrust in God during their wanderings in the desert.
Did you know? The suggestion to appoint a new leader and return to Egypt was a serious act of rebellion not only against Moses but also against God's leadership.
Did you know? Moses and Aaron falling on their faces is an act of prostration, prayer, and also a symbol of deep distress in the face of the people's rebellion.
Did you know? Joshua and Caleb tearing their clothes was a powerful expression of deep sorrow, but also a sign of protest against the spies' slander and the people's rebellion.
Did you know? Joshua and Caleb describe the inhabitants of the land as "our bread" – a metaphorical expression meaning they would be easy to conquer, just as food is easy to consume.

Did you know? The threat to stone with stones was a very severe capital punishment in biblical times, usually carried out for serious offenses like blasphemy or idolatry, showing the extent of the people's rage.
Did you know? God's question "How long will this people spurn Me?" expresses His frustration with the people's repeated rebellion and lack of faith, despite all the miracles they had witnessed.
Did you know? God's offer to Moses to make him into a great and mighty nation was a test of his leadership and devotion to his people, and Moses chose to pray for them instead.
Did you know? Moses reminds God that the nations know God is "seen eye to eye" among the people, an expression emphasizing the direct and unique connection between God and His people.
Did you know? Moses prays to God using the phrase "slow to anger and abundant in kindness," attributes that God Himself defined at Mount Sinai.
Did you know? The phrase "ten times" does not necessarily indicate an exact number, but rather a complete and ample number of times the people tested God's patience.
Did you know? Caleb son of Jephunneh received special praise from God for having "a different spirit with him," meaning a spirit of faith and courage unlike the other spies and the people.
Did you know? The punishment of 40 years of wandering in the desert was determined by the principle of "a day for a year," meaning one year for each of the 40 days the spies explored the land.
Did you know? The Ark of the Covenant and Moses did not go to battle with the people who decided to ascend the mountain, symbolizing that God was not with them in this reckless initiative.
